title: ISO/SOC2 Control Closure Roadmap & Auditor FAQ — RBAC v2 / Audit Logs / Evidence Automation / SIEM
content:
Executive summary:

This working brief lays out a pragmatic closure roadmap for controls tied to RBAC v2, the audit-log schema, evidence automation pipelines, and SIEM export. The goal is a small, auditable set of deliverables that bridge current implementation gaps for SOC 2 (TSC) and ISO 27001 control families and to prepare concise Q&A and evidence bundles for external auditors.

Context and scope:
- In scope: RBAC v2 rollout (role model + policy engine), canonical audit log schema (v3), evidence automation (collection/packaging/retention), SIEM export and monitoring feeds.
- Controls mapped: logical access controls, change management for access, system activity monitoring, secure logging and log retention, incident detection/response telemetry, and evidence retention for attestations.
- Audience: Security compliance owners, eng leads (serving-runtime, infra, SRE), and audit liaisons.

Mapping highlights (summary):
- RBAC v2 -> SOC 2: Logical access (CC6), Change control for privileged assignments -> ISO 27001: A.9 (Access control), A.12.2 (Change management)
- Audit log schema -> SOC 2: CC7 System operations / monitoring, Security event logging; ISO 27001: A.12.4 (Logging and monitoring), A.12.3 (Backup)
- Evidence automation -> SOC 2: Evidence of operating effectiveness (policies + sampled artifacts), ISO: Annex A control evidence alignment and audit trail retention
- SIEM export -> SOC 2: Continuous monitoring evidence / alerting, ISO: A.12.4 and A.16 (incident management)

Risk scoring and acceptance criteria (quick):
- Risk categories: Confidentiality, Integrity (tamper), Availability (loss of log retention), Compliance (missing evidence).
- Acceptance criteria per control: documented policy, implemented enforcement, tamper-evident logs, automated evidence packaging, 90-day retention for high-fidelity logs (configurable up to 2 years per class), and sample extraction tooling demonstrates reproducible exports.

Current gaps (top issues observed):
1) RBAC assignment auditability (GAP-001)
- Symptom: Role assignment events are created but not always correlated to requestor identity in the canonical log topic.
- Impact: Cannot prove change origin for privileged role grants; auditor will ask for chain-of-custody.
- Remediation: Add assignment_request_id and requestor_principal fields to RBAC audit events; backfill mapping for last 90 days using access-control-service logs.
- Owner: Platform engineering (access-control team)
- Target: 4 weeks for schema change + 2 weeks backfill.
- Evidence: event schema diff, backfill job run log, sample events.

2) Tamper-evidence and retention policy gaps for SIEM export (GAP-002)
- Symptom: Raw logs pushed to SIEM lack an immutable manifest and signed checksum metadata. Retention policy exists but proof of immutability is weak.
- Impact: Auditor will flag integrity of logs and long-term retention proof.
- Remediation: Ingest logs into S3 with versioning + object lock for high-fidelity event streams; publish daily signed manifest (KMS-signed) to artifact bucket; update SIEM export job to attach manifest reference.
- Owner: Observability team + infra-delivery
- Target: 6 weeks (incl. KMS policy changes)
- Evidence: sample signed manifest, S3 object lock config screenshot, SIEM export job config PR.

3) Evidence automation coverage and traceability (GAP-003)
- Symptom: Evidence bundles for controls are manually assembled; limited automated linkage between policy versions, deployment manifests, and proof-of-execution.
- Impact: Time-consuming audit response and risk of inconsistent evidence versions.
- Remediation: Implement an evidence builder lambda that consumes control-tags from CI/CD artifacts and auto-generates a zip with policy, PR link, deployment hash, timestamp, and verification script. Store artifact with deterministic key pattern.
- Owner: Security automation + release engineering
- Target: 5 weeks
- Evidence: sample evidence bundle, pipeline config, job run logs.

4) Audit log schema inconsistencies across services (GAP-004)
- Symptom: Several microservices use variants of the audit schema (timestamp formats, user id fields named differently), causing parsing errors in SIEM.
- Impact: Missing events in dashboards, incomplete alerting.
- Remediation: Publish canonical schema v3, release lightweight library for event construction, and run a compatibility scan with a central linter job; schedule service fixes.
- Owner: Developer experience + platform engineering
- Target: 3 weeks for library + 8 weeks for critical service fixes
- Evidence: canonical schema document, linter run output, PRs.

Closure roadmap (milestones):
- Week 0–2: Finalize schema v3 and RBAC audit event additions; produce the explicit mapping doc (control -> artifacts).
- Week 2–6: Implement signed manifests for SIEM export and S3 retention configuration.
- Week 4–8: Evidence automation pipeline development + test bundles for 6 representative controls.
- Week 6–12: Backfill audit events, run compatibility linter, stabilize service fixes.
- Week 10–14: Dry run auditor session (internal) using generated evidence bundles and scripted Q&A.

Operational acceptance checklist (what we must demonstrate to auditor):
- End-to-end example: role change request -> policy engine evaluation -> role grant event -> logged event with requestor_principal and assignment_request_id -> entry stored in S3 + SIEM export -> signed manifest published -> evidence bundle containing PR and pipeline run that led to the change.
- Auditability tests: reproducible extraction command, example hashes of artifacts, signed manifests for at least 30 days.
- Retention proof: object lock / versioning screenshots and bucket lifecycle policies.
- Monitoring: SIEM rule to detect high-risk role grants (alert -> incident ticket link).

Sample audit Q&A (prepared answers and evidence pointers):
Q1: How do you control and record privileged role assignments?
A1: RBAC v2 enforces role templates and approval flows. All assignment events include requestor_principal, approver_id (if applicable), assignment_request_id and a change hash. Events are emitted to the canonical audit topic and persisted to S3 with versioning. Evidence: canonical schema (confluence), sample event (s3://redwood-evidence-prod/sample-events/rbac-assignment.json), PR for RBAC change (github PR link), signed manifest for the day.

Q2: How can you prove logs were not altered after generation?
A2: We use S3 Object Lock on high-fidelity audit buckets for the configured retention class. Additionally, we publish a daily manifest file that contains SHA256 checksums for each partitioned log file; the manifest is KMS-signed with an auditable key rotation policy. Evidence: signed manifest sample, KMS rotation policy screenshot, S3 configurations.

Q3: What prevents truncation or loss in the SIEM export pipeline?
A3: The export job is consumer-group aware and emits per-batch delivery receipts to the export-monolith topic. We keep a delivery ledger with offsets and a reconciliation job that computes expected vs delivered counts daily; reconciliation alerts create a ticket if counts diverge beyond threshold. Evidence: reconciliation run output, export job config, ticket history for detected anomalies.

Q4: How do you ensure evidence bundles correspond to the exact code/config that produced production behavior?
A4: The evidence-builder includes the deployment artifact hash, CI pipeline run id, and the commit SHA. Bundles are deposited under deterministic keys (control-year/month/day/sha.zip), and each bundle includes a small verification script that replays the selector queries against archived logs. Evidence: sample bundle zip, verification run log.

Examples of artifacts to attach to auditor bundle (by control):
- RBAC / Access control: policy docs, role-change PRs, assignment event sample, access-control service logs
- Logging integrity: signed manifests, S3 object lock configs, KMS key metadata
- Monitoring: SIEM rule definitions, recent alert digests, reconciliation job runs
- Evidence automation: sample generated bundle, pipeline run id, storage path of artifact

Dry-run plan for internal auditor rehearsal:
- Day 0: Assemble evidence bundles for 6 controls (RBAC, logging, incident mgmt, change control, backup, privileged access).
- Day 1: 2-hour walkthrough with product-security + platform engineers; produce quick-fix tickets for any missing artifacts.
- Day 2: Full Q&A scripting with auditors (simulate 15–20 common questions) and produce a final evidence zip for external auditor handoff.

Appendix: short canonical audit event example (human-readable)
{
  time: 2025-10-12T15:23:12Z,
  event_type: ACCOUNT_ROLE_ASSIGNMENT,
  requestor_principal: user:liam.chen@redwood.ai,
  approver_id: user:marta.alvarez@redwood.ai,
  assignment_request_id: req-3f2b9,
  role: infra-admin,
  target_principal: service:ingest-collector,
  service: access-control,
  trace_id: 8e2a...
}

Notes / open questions for reviewers:
- Confirm retention classes (high-fidelity vs aggregated logs) and map to ISO control requirements (we currently plan 90 days / 365 days tiers).
- Decide whether evidence bundles should be stored in the same account as production or in a separate audit account with cross-account read roles.
- Confirm KMS key custodians and the auditable rotation schedule.

Next steps (owner action items):
- Ayesha K. to convene RBAC + Observability + Release Eng working session (by 2025-10-07).
- Platform eng to produce schema v3 PR and compatibility linter (due 2025-10-16).
- Observability to prototype signed manifest publish (due 2025-11-01).
- Security automation to stub evidence-builder and produce 6 sample bundles (due 2025-11-08).

End of brief.
